title: micro-sprint-catalog-alfred
content:
Purpose: compact personal ledger for quick micro-sprint experiments. Single-page reference I can update during tinkering sessions. Not a canonical record (push final results to the run DB), but good for quick decisions and reminders.

Legend/columns: run_id | date | model | seq | batch | quant | hw | median_lat_ms | cost_per_1k_tokens_est | perf_delta_vs_baseline | notes | todo

Quick table (comma-separated for fast paste into csv):
run_001,2025-09-12,redwood-v1-small,512,8,4-bit,rtx-a5000,34,0.72,-,initial sweep,check INF-4721
run_002,2025-09-12,redwood-v1-small,512,16,4-bit,rtx-a5000,46,0.51,+35% throughput after batch bump,verify stability on longer sequences
run_003,2025-09-15,redwood-v1-medium,1024,8,8-bit,rtx-a5000,92,1.95,baseline,good qual but expensive,add eval set A
run_004,2025-09-16,redwood-v1-medium,1024,12,8-bit,rtx-a5000,78,1.31,-15% latency vs baseline,try KV-cache prefix=800
run_005,2025-09-20,redwood-v1-small,2048,6,4-bit,rtx-a5000,120,1.10,regression on tail lat,look into attention-kernel
run_006,2025-09-25,redwood-v1-small,512,16,4-bit,rtx-a5000,44,0.48,+stable throughput after kernel patch,pr:github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/1284

Notes (free-form):
- Short-hands used: quant=quantization (4-bit, 8-bit), hw=hardware. cost_per_1k_tokens_est computed with quick unit costs from console (approx).
- When perf_delta_vs_baseline is '-', it's the chosen baseline for that model/seq slice.
- run_004 looked promising: latency down, quality unchanged on quick eval. Need to run eval set A and B overnight.
- run_005 shows tail-latency spikes on long seqs; hypothesize KV cache warmup + attention kernel mismatch. Patch candidate in my local branch.

To-do (short):
- [ ] push run_004 config into canary with 5% traffic (ticket INF-4721), tag config: canary-sprint-09
- [ ] automate cost_est calc from console export and replace manual numbers
- [ ] run full eval (A/B) for run_006 against baseline and upload artifacts to confluence
- [ ] add simple plot of median_lat_ms vs batch for model small (quick script in experiments/mini)

Quick diffs & heuristics I want to remember:
- If median_lat_ms < 50ms and cost_per_1k_tokens_est < $0.6 => candidate for opt tier
- If seq > 1024 AND median_lat_ms increases >30% => look at KV warmup + consider prefix cache warmup strategy
- Batch tuning: small model benefits up to batch=16 on a5000, then diminishing returns; medium model prefers 8-12 depending on seq.

Scratch snippets:
- shell: python tools/sim_cost.py --model redwood-v1-small --batch 16 --seq 512 --quant 4bit
- quick note: "if we quantize to 4-bit with kernel patch X, expect ~10-18% more tokens/sec on a5000; watch for quality drop on named-entity outputs"

References:
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime (look for thread starting Sep 12 re: micro-sprint kernel patch)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/1284 (kernel patch, unit tests passed)

Notes to self (end):
- Keep this sheet minimal. If table grows past ~30 rows, move to run-db with full metadata. Use this for quick mental model and next actions.
- When I hand off to Maya or Ravi, add a short summary at top and mark status -> in_review.
